trust_decision.summary: With :sanitize_html set, untrusted Textile input is scanned by the tag-matching regex in clean_html; the tag-name group \w* overlaps the following [^>]*? so unterminated tag-like input backtracks heavily (fix makes \w* possessive).

landing_point.why: Advisory names sanitize_html; clean_html is the only regex-based sanitizer and the only gsub on the full input.

fix_sites.module_kind: core library formatter (HTML output, sanitizer helper)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists; the only other regex on attacker data (html.rb:335) runs on a single bounded tag body with static prop names and is not super-linear in an obvious way.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Allowed tags with whitelisted attributes (a href/title, img src/alt, td colspan, closing and self-closing tags) must still be rebuilt; an over-broad fix (e.g. escaping all '<' or dropping attribute capture) breaks sanitize_html fixtures.

O6_input_shapes: unterminated tag start '<' + letter + long word/attribute run without '>'
repeated tag-like openers (with optional leading '/') without closing '>'

O8b_injection_room.sibling: attribute-extraction regex per allowed prop could be written with overlapping quantifiers (e.g. \s*=\s*(.*?\s*)+) over raw[3]
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same function parses attacker-controlled attribute text with an interpolated regex; a maintainer extending attribute parsing could plausibly write a backtracking form.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: javascript: scheme check in link/image could be a richer regex over href/src (e.g. whitespace/entity-tolerant) with nested quantifiers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Filter applies under the same sanitize_html flag to untrusted URLs; hardening against obfuscated schemes is a natural extension.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333) in an HTML sanitizer regex

O10_build.language: Ruby (+ C extension generated from Ragel)
O10_build.toolchain: Ruby, rake, rake-compiler, C compiler, ragel >= 6.3 to generate ext/redcloth_scan/*.c from ragel/*.rl (tasks/ragel_extension_task.rb:99-101)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make the tag-name quantifier possessive/atomic or cap input length in clean_html — which is essentially the published one-character fix.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/redcloth/formatters/html.rb:337 href/src scheme allowlist in clean_html is unanchored-case-sensitive (^(http|https|ftp):) — sanitization-quality question, not ReDoS; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell used); lib/ has ~8 Ruby files plus ragel sources, so tiny_repo (<5 MB) is likely but unconfirmed and not flagged.
Whether the possessive fix fully removes super-linear behaviour ([^>]*? still rescans to end per '<' start, likely O(n^2)) was not tested; no code was run.
Pure-Ruby scanner path (ragel/redcloth_scan.rb.rl:38) also calls before_transform; same sink, not a separate route.
